     3	description: "Generate a conference poster (article + tcbposter LaTeX → A0/A1 PDF + editable PPTX + SVG) from a compiled paper. Use when user says \"做海报\", \"制作海报\", \"conference poster\", \"make poster\", \"生成poster\", \"poster session\", or wants to create a poster for a conference presentation."
     4	argument-hint: [paper-directory-or-venue]
     5	allowed-tools: Bash(*), Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Agent, mcp__codex__codex, mcp__codex__codex-reply
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Paper Poster: From Paper to Conference Poster
     9	
    10	Generate a conference poster from: **$ARGUMENTS**
    11	
    12	## Context
    13	
    14	This skill runs **after** Workflow 3 (`/paper-writing`). It takes a compiled paper and generates a print-ready poster for conference poster sessions. The poster extracts key content from the paper — it does **not** dump the full paper text onto a poster.
    15	
    16	Unlike papers (dense prose, 8-15 pages), posters are **visual-first**: one page, 4 columns, bullet points only, figures dominant. A good poster tells the story in 60 seconds.
    17	
    18	## Constants
    19	
    20	- **VENUE = `NeurIPS`** — Target venue, determines color scheme. Supported: `NeurIPS`, `ICML`, `ICLR`, `AAAI`, `ACL`, `EMNLP`, `CVPR`, `ECCV`, `GENERIC`. Override via argument (e.g., `/paper-poster "— venue: ICML"`).
    21	- **POSTER_SIZE = `A0`** — Paper size. Options: `A0` (841x1189mm, default), `A1` (594x841mm).
    22	- **ORIENTATION = `landscape`** — Orientation. Options: `landscape` (default), `portrait`.
    23	- **COLUMNS = 4** — Number of content columns. Typical: 4 for landscape A0 (IMRAD), **3 for portrait A0** (research consensus), 2 for portrait A1. Portrait A0 should NEVER use 4 columns — text becomes too narrow and unreadable.
    24	- **PAPER_DIR = `paper/`** — Directory containing the compiled paper (main.tex + figures/).
    25	- **OUTPUT_DIR = `poster/`** — Output directory for all poster files.
    26	- **REVIEWER_MODEL = `gpt-5.4`** — Model used via Codex MCP for poster review.
    27	- **AUTO_PROCEED = false** — At each checkpoint, **always wait for explicit user confirmation**. Set `true` only if user explicitly requests fully autonomous mode.
    28	- **COMPILER = `latexmk`** — LaTeX build tool.
    29	- **ENGINE = `pdflatex`** — LaTeX engine. Use `xelatex` for CJK text.
    30	
    31	> 💡 Override: `/paper-poster "paper/" — venue: CVPR, size: A1, orientation: portrait, columns: 3`
    32	
    33	## Venue Color Schemes
    34	
    35	Use **deep, saturated** colors for primary — pastel/light colors wash out on large posters viewed from distance. Each venue uses a **3-color system**: primary (dark, for title bar), secondary (medium, for section headers), accent (contrast, for highlights).
    36	
    37	| Venue | Primary | Secondary | Accent | Background | Text |
    38	|-------|---------|-----------|--------|------------|------|
    39	| NeurIPS | `#4C1D95` (deep purple) | `#6D28D9` (purple) | `#2563EB` (blue) | `#F5F3FF` | `#1F2937` |
    40	| ICML | `#7F1D1D` (deep maroon) | `#B91C1C` (red) | `#1E40AF` (blue) | `#EDD5D5` | `#111827` |
    41	| ICLR | `#065F46` (deep green) | `#059669` (green) | `#0284C7` (blue) | `#F0FDF4` | `#1F2937` |
    42	| CVPR | `#1E3A8A` (deep blue) | `#2563EB` (blue) | `#7C3AED` (purple) | `#F8FAFC` | `#1F2937` |
    43	| AAAI | `#0C4A6E` (deep navy) | `#0369A1` (blue) | `#DC2626` (red) | `#F0F9FF` | `#1F2937` |
    44	| ACL | `#155E75` (deep teal) | `#0891B2` (teal) | `#7C3AED` (purple) | `#F0FDFA` | `#1F2937` |
    45	| EMNLP | `#713F12` (deep amber) | `#D97706` (amber) | `#2563EB` (blue) | `#FFFBEB` | `#1F2937` |
    46	| ECCV | `#701A75` (deep fuchsia) | `#C026D3` (fuchsia) | `#0891B2` (teal) | `#FDF4FF` | `#1F2937` |
    47	| GENERIC | `#1E293B` (deep slate) | `#334155` (slate) | `#2563EB` (blue) | `#F8FAFC` | `#1F2937` |
    48	
    49	> ⚠️ **Color lesson**: Never use light/pastel colors (e.g., `#8B5CF6`) as primary — they look washed out on A0 posters. Always use the darkest shade as primary for the title bar.
    50	
    51	## State Persistence (Compact Recovery)
    52	
    53	Poster generation can be long. Persist state to `poster/POSTER_STATE.json` after each phase:
    54	
    55	```json
    56	{
    57	  "phase": 3,
    58	  "venue": "NeurIPS",
    59	  "poster_size": "A0",
    60	  "orientation": "landscape",
    61	  "columns": 4,
    62	  "figures_selected": ["architecture.pdf", "results.pdf"],
    63	  "codex_thread_id": "019cfcf4-...",
    64	  "status": "in_progress",
    65	  "timestamp": "2026-03-18T15:00:00"
    66	}
    67	```
    68	
    69	**On startup**: if `POSTER_STATE.json` exists with `"status": "in_progress"` and within 24h → resume from saved phase. Otherwise → fresh start.
    70	
    71	## Critical LaTeX Architecture Decisions
    72	
    73	> ⚠️ **MUST use `article` class, NEVER `beamer` class.** The beamer class consumes too many TeX grouping levels for its overlay/mode system. Combined with tcbposter's `enhanced` style on 8+ posterboxes, this triggers `! TeX capacity exceeded, sorry [grouping levels=255]`. The article class + geometry package for custom page size is the correct approach. This was validated through 5 failed compilation attempts with beamer before switching to article.
    74	
    75	> ⚠️ **NEVER use `adjustbox` package.** It may not be installed in minimal TeX distributions. Use plain `\includegraphics[width=0.96\linewidth]{file}` instead. Do NOT use `max height` option (requires adjustbox).
    76	
    77	### Template Foundation
    78	
    79	```latex
    80	\documentclass{article}
    81	% A0 landscape: paperwidth=1189mm,paperheight=841mm
    82	% A0 portrait:  paperwidth=841mm,paperheight=1189mm
    83	\usepackage[paperwidth=1189mm,paperheight=841mm,margin=0mm]{geometry}
    84	\usepackage{tcolorbox}
    85	\tcbuselibrary{poster,skins,fitting}
    86	\usepackage{graphicx}
    87	\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
    88	\usepackage{enumitem}
    89	\usepackage[table]{xcolor}  % MUST use [table] option for \rowcolor in tables
    90	\usepackage{lmodern}
    91	\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
    92	\pagestyle{empty}
    93	```
    94	
    95	> ⚠️ **NEVER use `\usepackage[most]{tcolorbox}`** — it pulls in `listingsutf8.sty` which may not be installed. Always use `\tcbuselibrary{poster,skins,fitting}` explicitly.
    96	
    97	> ⚠️ **Use `[table]{xcolor}`** not plain `{xcolor}` — needed for `\rowcolor` in benchmark tables. The `colortbl` package is loaded automatically by this option.
    98	
    99	## tcbposter Layout Rules (Critical)
   100	
   101	> ⚠️ **The #1 cause of poster failures is content overflow.** tcbposter uses a fixed grid — content that exceeds the box is **silently clipped** with no compilation error. You will NOT see any warning; the poster will simply be cut off.
   102	
   103	> ⚠️ **The #2 cause is large whitespace gaps.** Using too few rows (e.g., `rows=5`) creates ~168mm per row on A0 landscape. If title text only needs 120mm, the remaining 48mm is wasted whitespace. Solution: use `rows=20` for fine-grained control (~42mm per row).
   104	
   105	### Grid System: `rows=20` (Critical)
   106	
   107	Use `rows=20` for A0 landscape. Each row ≈ 42mm, giving precise control over section heights.
   108	
   109	**Recommended row allocation for 4-column A0 landscape:**
   110	
   111	| Section | Rows | Height | Row range |
   112	|---------|:----:|:------:|-----------|
   113	| Title bar | 3 | ~126mm | `top` to `row4` |
   114	| Stat banner | 2 | ~84mm | `row4` to `row6` |
   115	| Body content | 14 | ~588mm | `row6` to `bottom` |
   116	
   117	**Key principle**: Always use `between=rowN and rowM` syntax (not `below=name`) for precise vertical placement. The `below=` syntax lets tcolorbox auto-place, which often leaves unwanted gaps.
   118	
   119	### Row Count Guidance
   120	
   121	| Poster Size | Orientation | Recommended rows | Columns | Row height |
   122	|-------------|-------------|:---:|:---:|:---:|
   123	| A0 | landscape | 20 | 4 | ~42mm |
   124	| A0 | portrait | 20 | **3** | ~59mm |
   125	| A1 | landscape | 16 | 3 | ~37mm |
   126	| A1 | portrait | 20 | 2 | ~30mm |
   127	
   128	### Portrait A0 Layout (3 columns, rows=20)
   129	
   130	> ⚠️ **Portrait A0 posters use 2-3 columns, NEVER 4.** Research consensus: "Two columns is typical for a poster with a portrait orientation" (Colin Purrington, NYU poster guides). At 841mm width, 4 columns give only ~195mm per column — too narrow for readable text at poster-session distance. **3 columns (~260mm each) is the recommended default** for content-rich papers. Use 2 columns for simpler posters or when figures need more horizontal space.
   131	
   132	For portrait posters (841x1189mm), use a **3-column, 3-row-band** layout:
   133	
   134	| Section | Rows | Row range | Content |
   135	|---------|:----:|-----------|---------|
   136	| Title bar | 4 | `top` to `row4` | Title + authors + venue (span=3) |
   137	| Stat banner | 2 | `row4` to `row6` | 3 headline stat callouts (span=3) |
   138	| Row A | 5 | `row6` to `row11` | Background+Motivation, Method (hero fig), Key Results (fig) |
   139	| Row B | 5 | `row11` to `row16` | Contributions, Equations+Ablation, Result 2 (fig+table) |
   140	| Row C | 4 | `row16` to `bottom` | References+QR, Setup+Benchmarks, Key Takeaways |
   141	
   142	**3-column portrait layout diagram:**
   143	```
   144	┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
   145	│         TITLE BAR (span=3)          │
   146	├─────────────────────────────────────┤
   147	│   Stat 1   │   Stat 2   │  Stat 3  │
   148	├────────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
   149	│ Background │  Method    │ Result 1 │
   150	│ & Motiv.   │ (hero fig) │ (figure) │
   151	├────────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
   152	│ Contribu-  │ Equations  │ Result 2 │
   153	│ tions      │ & Ablation │ (fig+tbl)│
   154	├────────────┼────────────┼──────────┤
   155	│ References │  Setup &   │   Key    │
   156	│ + QR Code  │ Benchmarks │Takeaways │
   157	└────────────┴────────────┴──────────┘
   158	```
   159	
   160	> ⚠️ **All 3 columns in each row band share the same row boundaries.** This ensures cross-column alignment. Never mix `row6 to row11` in one column with `row6 to row10` in another — it creates visual misalignment.
   161	
   162	> ⚠️ **Use `spacing=0mm`** for tight layouts. Card separation is handled by card styles (left accent stripe, drop shadow), not grid spacing. Grid spacing > 2mm creates visible gaps between rows.
   163	
   164	### Modern Card Design System (Left Accent Stripe)
   165	
   166	Instead of rounded boxes with colored headers, use a **left accent stripe** design. This is cleaner, more modern, and avoids the "PowerPoint box" look.
   167	
   168	Define **4 card styles** using the venue's 3-color system:
   169	
   170	```latex
   171	% Tinted card backgrounds (NOT pure white — adds warmth)
   172	\definecolor{redbg}{HTML}{FFF5F3}     % warm pink tint for redcard
   173	\definecolor{bluebg}{HTML}{F0F4FF}    % cool blue tint for bluecard
   174	\definecolor{darkbg}{HTML}{FDF6F3}    % warm cream tint for darkcard
   175	\definecolor{redtitlebg}{HTML}{FDEAE8}   % title bar tint
   176	\definecolor{bluetitlebg}{HTML}{E4ECFF}
   177	\definecolor{darktitlebg}{HTML}{F5E8E2}
   178	
   179	\tcbset{
   180	  redcard/.style={
   181	    enhanced, arc=0pt, boxrule=0pt, colback=redbg,
   182	    borderline west={5pt}{0pt}{secondary},
   183	    left=16pt, right=14pt, top=4pt, bottom=4pt,
   184	    fonttitle=\fontsize{40}{48}\selectfont\bfseries\color{secondary},
   185	    coltitle=secondary, colbacktitle=redtitlebg,
   186	    toptitle=6pt, bottomtitle=6pt,
   187	    titlerule=2pt, titlerule style={secondary!50},
   188	    valign=top, drop shadow={opacity=0.18},
   189	  },
   190	  bluecard/.style={...same pattern with accent color and bluebg...},
   191	  darkcard/.style={...same pattern with primary color and darkbg...},
   192	  highlightcard/.style={
   193	    enhanced, arc=0pt, boxrule=0pt, colback=primary!18!white,
   194	    borderline west={6pt}{0pt}{primary},
   195	    fonttitle=...\color{white}, colbacktitle=primary,
   196	    ...
   197	  },
   198	}
   199	```
   200	
   201	**Card assignment pattern** (creates visual rhythm):
   202	- **redcard** (secondary stripe): Background, Key Idea, Ablation, References, Setup
   203	- **bluecard** (accent stripe): Result 1, Result 2, Benchmarks, Analysis
   204	- **darkcard** (primary stripe): Contributions, Method
   205	- **highlightcard** (primary fill): Key Takeaways / Conclusion
   206	
   207	> ⚠️ **Card backgrounds must NOT be pure white (#FFFFFF).** Use subtle tints matching the card's color family. Pure white cards on a tinted poster background look disconnected. The tint should be barely visible but adds cohesion.
   208	
   209	### Figure + Caption Macro
   210	
   211	Define a consistent macro for all figures to ensure uniform spacing:
   212	
   213	```latex
   214	\newcommand{\posterfig}[3]{%
   215	  \centering\includegraphics[width=#1\linewidth]{#2}\\[3mm]
   216	  {\fontsize{26}{32}\selectfont\color{textgray}\textit{#3}}\vspace{2mm}%
   217	}
   218	% Usage: \posterfig{0.96}{figures/results.png}{Caption text here.}
   219	```
   220	
   221	> ⚠️ **Inconsistent figure-text spacing** is the #1 visual flaw in generated posters. The `\posterfig` macro enforces uniform 3mm gap + 2mm bottom padding across all figures.
   222	
   223	### Content Colorbox Intensity
   224	
   225	Inside cards, use `\colorbox{color!N}` for highlighted blocks. The intensity `N` must be **18-25%** (not 8-12% which is too faint):
   226	
   227	```latex
   228	% TOO FAINT (invisible on print):
   229	\colorbox{primary!8}{\parbox{...}{...}}
   230	
   231	% CORRECT (visible, distinct):
   232	\colorbox{primary!20}{\parbox{0.94\linewidth}{...}}
   233	\colorbox{accent!20}{\parbox{0.94\linewidth}{...}}
   234	\colorbox{secondary!20}{\parbox{0.94\linewidth}{...}}
   235	```
   236	
   237	Similarly, `\rowcolor` in tables should use 15% intensity: `\rowcolor{primary!15}`.
   238	
   239	### Font Size Rules (A0 at article class — NO scale factor)
   240	
   241	> ⚠️ **Critical**: When using `article` class (not beamerposter), there is NO automatic scale factor. All font sizes are literal. A poster viewed from 1.5m needs much larger fonts than you think.
   242	
   243	| Element | Font size | Leading | Example |
   244	|---------|:---------:|:-------:|---------|
   245	| Title | 90pt | 108pt | `\fontsize{90}{108}\selectfont` |
   246	| Author line | 42pt | 50pt | `\fontsize{42}{50}\selectfont` |
   247	| Section headers | 42pt | 50pt | via `fonttitle=\fontsize{42}{50}...` |
   248	| Sub-headers | 38pt | 46pt | `\subheader{}{}` command |
   249	| Body text | 34pt | 44pt | `\fontsize{34}{44}\selectfont` |
   250	| Stat callout numbers | 72pt | 86pt | `\fontsize{72}{86}\selectfont` |
   251	| Stat callout labels | 30pt | 36pt | `\fontsize{30}{36}\selectfont` |
   252	| Equations | 32pt | 40pt | `\fontsize{32}{40}\selectfont` |
   253	| Table cells | 30pt | 38pt | `\fontsize{30}{38}\selectfont` |
   254	| Figure captions | 28pt | 34pt | `\fontsize{28}{34}\selectfont` |
   255	| References | 30pt | 40pt | `\fontsize{30}{40}\selectfont` |
   256	
   257	> ⚠️ **Lesson learned from testing**: Body text at 20pt on A0 is unreadable from more than 0.5m. 34pt is the minimum for comfortable reading at poster-session distance.
   258	
   259	### Content Budget
   260	
   261	**Total target: 300-500 words** (excluding figure captions and stat callout numbers).
   262	
   263	> ⚠️ **The #1 content mistake is too much text.** A poster is NOT a paper summary — it's a visual guide. Each bullet should be a **key phrase** (5-8 words), not a sentence. If you find yourself writing full sentences, you're putting too much text.
   264	
   265	> ⚠️ **Content density calibration**: When in doubt, use LESS text. It's much easier to add a few words than to trim dense paragraphs. Target ~70% fill per card (some breathing room), NOT 100%.
   266	
   267	| Box type | Max bullets | Max words | Figure? | Style |
   268	|----------|:-:|:-:|---------|-------|
   269	| Background | 3 | 40-60 | No | Short bullets + 1 key insight colorbox |
   270	| Key Idea / Architecture | 0-1 | 20-30 | Yes (hero fig) | Figure dominant + 2 one-liner colorboxes |
   271	| Contributions | 3-4 | 60-80 | No | Numbered, 1 line each |
   272	| Method | 2-3 | 40-60 | No | 2 equation colorboxes + 3 short bullets |
   273	| Results (each) | 2-3 | 30-50 | Yes (figure) | Figure + 2-3 one-line colorboxes |
   274	| Ablation | 3 | 30-40 | No | 3 colorboxes, 2 lines each max |
   275	| Analysis | 3 | 30-50 | Yes (figure) | Figure + 3 one-line colorboxes |
   276	| References | 4-5 | 30-40 | No | Author (year). Short title. *Venue* |
   277	| Setup | 4-5 | 30-40 | No | 5 one-liner colorboxes |
   278	| Benchmarks | 0 | 20 | No | Table + 1-line caption |
   279	| Key Takeaways | 3 | 30-40 | No | 3 short items + code link |
   280	
   281	**Bullet point rules:**
   282	- Maximum **8 words per bullet** when possible
   283	- Use `$\Rightarrow$` and `$\to$` for causal arrows instead of words
   284	- Numbers > words: "**42% less memory**" not "reduces memory usage by 42 percent"
   285	- Colorbox labels: "**vs. Depth:** 4L CoE ≈ 12L MoE, **42% less memory**" (one line)
   286	
   287	### Recommended 4-Column IMRAD Layout
   288	
   289	```
   290	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   291	│                    TITLE BAR (span=4)                     │
   292	│     Title (90pt) + Authors (42pt) + Venue + GitHub        │
   293	├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   294	│  Stat 1  │  Stat 2  │  Stat 3  │  Stat 4  │  STAT BANNER│
   295	├──────────┼──────────┼──────────┼──────────┤             │
   296	│Background│ Dataset  │Architectu│ Result 2 │             │
   297	│    &     │    &     │   re     │  + Table │             │
   298	│Motivation│Paradigms │ Overview │  + Stats │             │
   299	│    +     │  + Fig   │  + Fig   │  + Fig   │             │
   300	│Contributi│          │──────────│──────────│             │
   301	│   ons    │──────────│ Result 1 │ Ablation │             │
   302	│──────────│Computat. │  + Fig   │──────────│             │
   303	│References│ Models   │  + Table │Conclusion│             │
   304	│ + QR Code│+ Equations│ + Bullets│ + Future │             │
   305	└──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
   306	```
   307	
   308	## Workflow
   309	
   310	### Phase 0: Input Validation & Setup
   311	
   312	1. **Check prerequisites**:
   313	   ```bash
   314	   which pdflatex && which latexmk
   315	   ```
   316	
   317	   **If LaTeX is NOT installed**, try in order:
   318	   ```bash
   319	   # Option 1: brew cask (requires sudo — may fail in non-interactive shells)
   320	   brew install --cask mactex-no-gui
   321	
   322	   # Option 2: BasicTeX (smaller, may still need sudo)
   323	   brew install --cask basictex
   324	
   325	   # Option 3: User-directory install (NO sudo needed — always works)
   326	   curl -L https://mirror.ctan.org/systems/texlive/tlnet/install-tl-unx.tar.gz | tar xz
   327	   cd install-tl-*
   328	   cat > texlive.profile << 'PROF'
   329	   selected_scheme scheme-basic
   330	   TEXDIR ~/texlive/YYYY
   331	   TEXMFLOCAL ~/texlive/texmf-local
   332	   TEXMFSYSCONFIG ~/texlive/YYYY/texmf-config
   333	   TEXMFSYSVAR ~/texlive/YYYY/texmf-var
   334	   TEXMFHOME ~/texmf
   335	   binary_x86_64-darwin 1
   336	   instopt_adjustpath 0
   337	   instopt_adjustrepo 1
   338	   instopt_write18_restricted 1
   339	   tlpdbopt_autobackup 1
   340	   tlpdbopt_install_docfiles 0
   341	   tlpdbopt_install_srcfiles 0
   342	   PROF
   343	   ./install-tl --profile=texlive.profile
   344	   export PATH="$HOME/texlive/YYYY/bin/universal-darwin:$PATH"
   345	   ```
   346	
   347	   After installation, install required packages:
   348	   ```bash
   349	   tlmgr install tcolorbox pgf etoolbox environ trimspaces \
   350	     type1cm pdfcol tikzfill latexmk lm enumitem geometry
   351	   ```
   352	
   353	   > ⚠️ **Lesson learned**: `brew install --cask mactex-no-gui` often fails in non-interactive shells because the macOS installer requires sudo password. The user-directory TeX Live install (Option 3) always works without sudo.
   354	
   355	   > ⚠️ **Do NOT install or use `beamerposter`**. The article class approach does not need it.
   356	
   357	2. **Verify paper exists**:
   358	   ```bash
   359	   ls $PAPER_DIR/main.tex || ls $PAPER_DIR/main.pdf
   360	   ls $PAPER_DIR/sections/*.tex
   361	   ls $PAPER_DIR/figures/
   362	   ```
   363	
   364	3. **Backup existing poster**: if `poster/` exists, copy to `poster-backup-{timestamp}/`
   365	
   366	4. **Create output directory**: `mkdir -p poster/figures`
   367	
   368	5. **Copy figures** to poster directory:
   369	   ```bash
   370	   # IMPORTANT: Use cp, NOT ln -sf (symlinks)
   371	   # pdflatex often fails to resolve symlinks across directories
   372	   cp paper/figures/selected_figure.pdf poster/figures/
   373	   ```
   374	
   375	   > ⚠️ **Never use symlinks** for poster figures. `pdflatex` cannot reliably follow symlinks across directories. Always `cp` the actual files.
   376	
   377	6. **Convert PDF figures to PNG** for PPTX embedding:
   378	   ```bash
   379	   python3 -c "import pdf2image" 2>/dev/null || pip install pdf2image
   380	   # For each figure:
   381	   python3 -c "
   382	   from pdf2image import convert_from_path
   383	   for name in ['paradigm', 'architecture', 'results', 'hallucination']:
   384	       imgs = convert_from_path(f'poster/figures/{name}.pdf', dpi=300)
   385	       imgs[0].save(f'poster/figures/{name}.png', 'PNG')
   386	   "
   387	   ```
   388	
   389	   > ⚠️ **python-pptx CANNOT embed PDF images.** You MUST convert to PNG first. This is a hard limitation of the OOXML format. Always generate PNG copies at 300 DPI during setup.
   390	
   391	7. **Detect CJK**: if paper contains Chinese/Japanese/Korean text, set ENGINE to `xelatex`
   392	
   393	8. **Check for resume**: read `poster/POSTER_STATE.json` if it exists
   394	
   395	### Phase 1: Content Extraction
   396	
   397	Read each section from `paper/sections/*.tex` and extract poster-appropriate content:
   398	
   399	**Extraction rules** — a poster shows ~30-40% of the paper's content:
   400

  1034	## Key Rules
  1035	
  1036	### Architecture
  1037	- **MUST use article class, NEVER beamer.** Beamer + tcbposter with 8+ enhanced boxes triggers `grouping levels=255` overflow. This is an architectural constraint, not fixable by style tweaks.
  1038	- **NEVER use adjustbox package.** Use plain `\includegraphics[width=...]` only.
  1039	- **NEVER use `\usepackage[most]{tcolorbox}`.** It pulls `listingsutf8.sty` which may not be installed. Use `\tcbuselibrary{poster,skins,fitting}` explicitly.
  1040	- **Use `[table]{xcolor}`** not `{xcolor}` — needed for `\rowcolor` in tables.
  1041	
  1042	### Layout
  1043	- **`rows=20` and `spacing=0mm`** for tight layout. Card separation via left accent stripe + drop shadow, not grid spacing.
  1044	- **Use `between=rowN and rowM` positioning.** Not `below=name` which leaves auto-sized gaps.
  1045	- **All columns in a row band share identical row boundaries.** Never mix `row6-row11` in col 1 with `row6-row10` in col 2.
  1046	- **Adjust row distribution to match content density.** After trimming text, reduce row allocation proportionally. Cards with `valign=top` show all whitespace at the bottom.
  1047	
  1048	### Content
  1049	- **Less text is more.** Target 300-500 words total. Each bullet: 5-8 words max. If it reads like a sentence, it's too long.
  1050	- **Do NOT fabricate data.** All numbers must come from `paper/sections/*.tex`.
  1051	- **No abstract paragraph.** Replace with stat banner (3-4 big-number callout boxes).
  1052	- **Figures should occupy 40-50% of poster area.** Posters are visual-first.
  1053	- **Use `\posterfig` macro** for all figures to ensure consistent spacing.
  1054	- **References: author (year). Short title. *Venue*** — no full titles.
  1055	- **De-AI polish**: Remove watch words (delve, pivotal, underscore, noteworthy, leverage, facilitate, harness).
  1056	
  1057	### Color & Design
  1058	- **Card backgrounds must NOT be pure white.** Use subtle tints (e.g., `#FFF5F3`, `#F0F4FF`) that match each card's color family.
  1059	- **Poster background should be tinted** (e.g., `#EDD5D5` for ICML red theme), not white or near-white.
  1060	- **Colorbox intensity: 18-25%**, not 8-12%. Faint colorboxes are invisible on print.
  1061	- **Left accent stripe card design** (`borderline west={5pt}{0pt}{color}`) — cleaner than rounded colored boxes.
  1062	- **4 card styles** (redcard/bluecard/darkcard/highlightcard) create visual rhythm across the poster.
  1063	
  1064	### Equations
  1065	- **Use `$\displaystyle ...$` inside colorboxes**, NOT `\[...\]`. Display math adds margins causing overfull hbox.
  1066	- **Reduce equation font to 26-28pt** inside narrow colorboxes.
  1067	- **Wrap equations in `\centering` + `\parbox{0.92\linewidth}`** for proper alignment.

  1070	- **Copy figures, never symlink.** `cp` not `ln -sf`. pdflatex can't follow symlinks.
